evals.name: both-declarative
evals.prompt: Create a Python pub/sub app named order-flow. One FastAPI service publishes an OrderPlaced event on the orders topic - order id, customer id, amount and the time it was placed, identified by the order id - and another logs each order it receives.
evals.expected_output: An order-flow uv workspace with contracts, publisher and subscriber packages built from the domain in the prompt, a declarative subscription (default) with a Dapr-free subscriber, a handler that drops invalid messages, a successful uv sync, a README.md and the exact final message plus the Dev Dashboard recommendation.
expectations: The root pyproject.toml has a [tool.uv.workspace] table with members contracts, publisher and subscriber
subscriber/pyproject.toml lists neither dapr nor dapr-ext-fastapi as a dependency
subscriber/main.py has @app.post("/events/pubsub/orders") with a parameter typed dict = Body( and contains no DaprApp
subscriber/handler.py returns "DROP" when pydantic raises ValidationError
resources/subscription.yaml has scopes containing order-flow-subscriber, matching the appID in dapr.yaml
dapr.yaml has appID order-flow-publisher with appPort 8001 and daprHTTPPort 3501, and appID order-flow-subscriber with appPort 8002 and daprHTTPPort 3502
The publisher calls publish_event( with data_content_type="application/json"
The agent ran uv sync --all-packages in the project root and it succeeded

The agent restated the resolved event, topic, fields and identifying field before creating any file, and no generated file contains an unresolved placeholder such as <EventName>, <TopicName> or <id_field>
The agent ran `diagrid-dev-dashboard --version` once and did not stop, ask or install because of the result

order-flow/README.md has sections for running and trying the app, the Diagrid Dapr Dev Dashboard (link https://github.com/diagridio/dev-dashboard) and running with Catalyst, plus a Switching the message broker paragraph that links https://docs.dapr.io/reference/components-reference/supported-pubsub/ and keeps metadata.name pubsub

The final output starts with exactly: The order-flow pub/sub application is created. Open the README.md file in the order-flow folder for a summary and instructions for running locally. followed only by the matching Diagrid Dapr Dev Dashboard recommendation

evals.name: programmatic-publisher-ttl-raw
evals.prompt: Create a Python pub/sub app named Notifier with a programmatic subscription (dapr-ext-fastapi). It publishes an AlertRaised event on the alerts topic - alert id, severity and message, identified by the alert id - the subscriber logs each alert, and the publisher sends messages with a 60-second TTL and as raw payload.
evals.expected_output: A Notifier workspace with a DaprApp-based programmatic subscriber for the alerts topic using a dead-letter topic and raw payload metadata, a publisher with string-valued TTL and rawPayload metadata, and a handler that decodes data_base64.
expectations: The subscriber code contains DaprApp(app) exactly once
The .subscribe( call has dead_letter_topic= and metadata={"rawPayload": "true"}
The publisher passes publish_metadata equal to {"ttlInSeconds": "60", "rawPayload": "true"} with string values, not an integer 60 or boolean true
subscriber/handler.py decodes data_base64 (base64.b64decode)
subscriber/pyproject.toml depends on dapr-ext-fastapi==1.18.3
No resources/subscription.yaml is created, and no file contains isRawPayload
The agent asked no question about the subscription type, because the prompt specified programmatic
The contract is the AlertRaised model from the prompt on the alerts topic, with alerts-deadletter as the dead-letter topic; no file mentions OrderPlaced or a topic named orders

evals.name: streaming-subscriber
evals.prompt: Create a Python streaming subscriber for the orders topic named Shipping.
evals.expected_output: A single-role streaming subscriber with subscribe_with_handler, a dead-letter topic, a handler that always returns a TopicEventResponse, a close in finally, no FastAPI/uvicorn and no appPort in dapr.yaml.
expectations: A streaming.py file calls subscribe_with_handler( with dead_letter_topic=, and every return path of handle_message returns a TopicEventResponse
main.py calls the close function returned by the subscription inside a finally block
The subscriber pyproject.toml lists neither fastapi nor uvicorn
The subscriber entry in dapr.yaml has no appPort key
No resources/subscription.yaml is created

The final output starts with exactly: The Shipping pub/sub application is created. Open the README.md file in the Shipping folder for a summary and instructions for running locally. followed only by the Diagrid Dapr Dev Dashboard recommendation

evals.name: edge-programmatic-routing
evals.prompt: Create a Python pub/sub subscriber project named OrderRisk using programmatic subscriptions. It subscribes to OrderPlaced events on the orders topic - order id, customer id and amount, identified by the order id - logs each one, routes orders with an amount over 1000 to a separate handler called `large`, and uses Kafka.
evals.expected_output: The agent explains that dapr-ext-fastapi cannot route by content and offers a declarative subscription instead (default yes). The project is named OrderRisk (folder OrderRisk, app ids order-risk-*). The result is a declarative subscription.yaml with a CEL rule and a /events/pubsub/orders/large route, and no programmatic subscription for orders.
expectations: transcript.md or final_message.md contains the question text "dapr-ext-fastapi cannot route by content. Use a declarative subscription for this topic instead?" (key phrase: cannot route by content ... declarative subscription), with the default answer logged as yes, and this appears in the transcript before the first project file or folder is created
After the default answer, resources/subscription.yaml has a rule whose match contains int(event.data.amount) > 1000 and whose path is /events/pubsub/orders/large
The subscriber has a route for /events/pubsub/orders/large and no file contains a DaprApp(...).subscribe registration for the orders topic
resources/subscription.yaml scopes contain order-risk-subscriber, matching the appID order-risk-subscriber in dapr.yaml (the kebab-case form of the project name OrderRisk)

resources/pubsub.yaml is a component of type pubsub.redis, and the README says: You asked for Kafka; this scaffold runs on Redis locally so it works without extra infrastructure, and explains how to switch by replacing the pubsub component file with a pubsub.kafka component

evals.name: no-domain-must-ask
evals.prompt: Create a Python pub/sub app named Signals.
evals.expected_output: The agent asks what the application publishes before it creates anything: the event and its topic, the message fields and which one identifies a message, and what the subscriber should do with it. It does not invent a domain and does not fall back to an order-processing example.
expectations: Before any file or folder is created, the agent asks which event the application publishes and on which topic
Before any file or folder is created, the agent asks which fields the message carries and which single field uniquely identifies it
Before any file or folder is created, the agent asks what the subscriber should do when it receives the event
The transcript shows no mkdir, no uv init and no file write before those domain questions are answered
The transcript contains none of OrderPlaced, ORDERS_TOPIC, handle_order_event, orders-deadletter or a topic named orders: the prompt names no domain and the skill must not invent one
The wiring questions (role and subscription type) may still be asked; the project name is not asked again, because the prompt already gives it as Signals
